chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
All the teeth are equal; for each tooth is five hundred dirhams.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for damaging a tooth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the uniformity of blood money (diyah) for injury to any tooth, valuing each at five hundred dirhams, which reflects the Shia juristic principle of equal compensation for similar functional units regardless of position. It underscores the precision of early Shia legal codification in personal injury cases, ensuring equitable treatment in financial reparation. This ruling is often cited in discussions regarding the consistency of diyah calculations across different types of bodily injuries.
